stage1.impression: A violet horn-shaped lamp on a walnut sideboard throws a big arched shadow across a pink-washed wall, and the shape and the shadow make a real graphic idea. But it reads as CG. The wall and the left object look smeared by the denoiser, like an oil painting. A magenta cast covers everything. The cropped purple slab on the left reads as a TV, not a loudspeaker, and the sideboard front falls into black. Nothing says dusk, and the throat glows cold blue-white against a warm room.

blocking_9: No denoiser smearing: the wall gradient and the shadow arc show fine, even grain or none at all, with no painterly blotches (wall 1200-1600 x 100-500, left object 0-240 x 50-560)
The loudspeaker reads at once as a tall acrylic horn, with its whole silhouette or a deliberate crop, not a dark slab cut by the frame edge
Dusk is visible: a cool blue window or sky light in frame or on the objects, against the lamp's warm light
The lamp is the brightest and most luminous thing in the frame: the wall above the shade is not brighter than the shade's glow, and the throat does not clip
Shadows keep detail: the sideboard front and the lower left are not crushed (crush_pct under 25)
The colour balance reads as warm lamplight through violet acrylic, not an overall magenta grade on a white wall

defects.what: Denoiser smearing: the wall gradient and the shadow arc have a blotchy, painterly look (64 samples)
The loudspeaker is cut by the frame and reads as a purple TV or monitor; its blotchy reflections look like a render
The left cabinet and the speaker's base are an unreadable dark purple mass (crush 41%)
The slatted front of the sideboard is crushed to black (crush 70.5%, median lum 2)
The opal sleeve clips (19.5%) and reads blue-white (B 247 > R 218), against the warm 2700 K spec and the warm wall
The wall above the shade is the brightest area in the frame (median lum 199) and pulls the eye above the product
The white wall (#EEE9E1) renders saturated pink (R245 G186 B194): the whole frame reads as a magenta grade
No window or dusk sky is visible: the dusk story does not read
The violet shadow band on the right runs off-frame and ends abruptly: a large, distracting shape

changes.problem: The image is visibly denoised to mush: the wall, the shadow arc and the speaker's acrylic look painted.

evidence.measured: Seen at 1:1: blotchy low-frequency patches on a flat wall; render.samples is 64

change.to: 512 (keep the denoiser, fed albedo and normal passes)

changes.expected: Smooth, continuous wall gradients and the shadow arc's penumbra; the acrylic's reflections become crisp shapes instead of smudges

changes.problem: The loudspeaker, the context piece, is cut down to a dark slab at the frame edge that reads as a TV.

evidence.measured: Only about 240 px of its width is in frame; median lum 21, crush 11%

change.to: 35 mm; [0.25,-1.80,1.05]; [0.10,0.45,0.95]; speaker [-0.30,0.50,0], so the speaker's full horn stands, softly defocused, in the left third and the lamp sits on the right third

changes.expected: The speaker's silhouette, from bell to stand, reads at a glance, and the lamp keeps hero scale and focus

changes.problem: Nothing in the frame says dusk: the 'room at dusk' is only lamplight on a pink wall.

evidence.measured: No window in frame; the sky's cool light hardly registers (left region B median 33, all near black)

change.to: 6.0, and frame part of the left window (along 0.9) behind the speaker so a blue-dusk pane and a cool rim on the speaker's acrylic are visible

changes.expected: A warm/cool contrast: a blue rim and sky on the left, the warm lamp pool on the right; the speaker's edges glow cool

changes.problem: The lamp's throat clips and reads cold blue-white, so it looks like a fluorescent tube, not a warm glow.
changes.expected: The sleeve shows a soft opal gradient with no flat white block, and stays the brightest object in the frame

changes.problem: The sideboard's slatted front and the lower left are crushed to black, which reads as a cheap render.

change.to: 0.12 (keep its cool colour, and drop elevation_deg from 20 to 8 so it reaches the cabinet front)

changes.expected: The walnut slats show grain and separation in deep shadow; the room stays low-key

changes.problem: The wall above the shade is brighter than the shade, so the eye goes to empty wall.

evidence.measured: lum_median 199 against 126 on the shade's flare (560-1060 x 380-510)

changes.expected: The wall hot spot falls below the shade's glow; the shade becomes the luminous centre

changes.problem: The off-white wall renders as saturated pink, so the whole image reads as a magenta grade rather than violet light on a warm-white room.

evidence.measured: R 245 G 186 B 194 on a wall specified as #EEE9E1

changes.expected: The wall away from the shade's tint reads warm cream; violet stays in the shade, its shadow and its transmitted light

changes.problem: The right half of the shade's shadow runs off the frame as a heavy violet band that competes with the lamp.

evidence.measured: Seen: a hard dark band cut by the frame edge

change.to: [0.36, 0.38, 0.68] (7 cm off the wall, so the shadow arc grows softer and wider)

changes.expected: A softer, more diffuse arch of shadow that frames the lamp without a hard band at the edge

out_of_scope.request: The opal sleeve shows through the shade as a hard rectangular block
out_of_scope.why: The sleeve and the shade are product parts; only the LED output (c4) can change
